label: PF Backlog 424
title: A1: canonical contracts (thin) + Go<->Python contract
body: [A1] ProductSpec, TechnologyProfile, RuntimeProfile, DeploymentProfile, LicenseProfile, EntitlementProfile, ComponentManifest, BOM, Evidence + the Go<->Python boundary contract. Grow by need; emit from existing code.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/execution_contract.py, core/skill_contracts.py, core/task_contract.py into thin canonical contracts (ProductSpec, TechnologyProfile, RuntimeProfile, DeploymentProfile, LicenseProfile, EntitlementProfile, ComponentManifest, BOM, Evidence) plus Go<->Python boundary schema. Emit from existing code paths; grow by need.
conflict_findings: Contract changes to skill_contracts.py may collide with concurrent API foundation work (BI-PF-0336)
duplication_findings: core/skill_contracts.py and core/task_contract.py already encode similar contract patterns — reuse shapes
Overlaps BI-PF-0336 (canonical api/ foundation) on where contracts live
BI-PF-0340 ENG-1 engineering task contract overlaps task-related contract fields
analysis.rationale: Thin, code-emitted contracts with strong existing reuse; low rewrite risk once BI-PF-0392 settles the foundation.
assumptions: BI-PF-0392 completed and defines api/ home
Contracts emitted from existing Python code, not authored in isolation
risks: Over-specifying thin contracts early leads to churn
Go<->Python boundary contract premature if Go core not started
missing_info: Location convention (api/ vs core/) after BI-PF-0392
Go<->Python transport mechanism (JSON file, gRPC, stdio)

context_review.reason: Thin contracts can be emitted from existing code once BI-PF-0392 settles.

brief.problem: Epic A needs a stable contract surface so the Go host and Python core can interoperate without coupling.
brief.what_adds: A1 — thin canonical contracts: ProductSpec, TechnologyProfile, RuntimeProfile, DeploymentProfile, LicenseProfile, EntitlementProfile, ComponentManifest, BOM, Evidence, plus the Go<->Python contract.
brief.why: Contract-first is the seam that lets new (Go) and existing (Python) code coexist and be packaged per edition.
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.

objective: A1 — thin canonical contracts: ProductSpec, TechnologyProfile, RuntimeProfile, DeploymentProfile, LicenseProfile, EntitlementProfile, ComponentManifest, BOM, Evidence, plus the Go<->Python contract.
acceptance_criteria: Go host and Python core exchange a valid payload
approach: Define the minimal typed contracts (Python dataclasses / schema) and the Go<->Python wire contract; keep them thin and grow only by need.
verification: Go host and Python core exchange a valid payload
